texts: Agent Galaxy is a 3D star-map of every published agent, placed by meaning. Type what you want in plain language and the map flies to the closest ones. three.ws/galaxy
Proximity is similarity: agents that do similar things sit near each other, so browsing the map is browsing by meaning rather than by keyword.
Instead of guessing keywords, you describe what you want in plain language and the same embedding model that placed the stars finds the closest ones.

issues.problem: The image shows roughly 600 small stars but only about ten of them carry text labels, so 'hundreds of labelled agent stars' overstates what is visible. Alt text must describe what is actually in the frame.
issues.fix: Use: "The Agent Galaxy page: 600 agent stars in 8 constellations clustered in 3D space, with the natural-language search box over them."

issues.problem: Post 3 restates the mechanism of post 1 almost word for word ('in plain language', 'the closest ones') and post 2 already covered 'rather than by keyword'. The thread ends on repetition instead of new information.
issues.fix: Acceptable as is, but if revised, post 3 could add the one new verified fact: the same embedding model placed the stars and ranks the query, which is already stated. Alternatively drop post 3 and ship posts 1 and 2.
